html:
A town of houses on stilts on Lake Nokoue in southern Benin, founded in the 18th century by the Tofinu people seeking refuge from the slave-raiding armies of Dahomey.

According to tradition the Fon warriors were forbidden by their religion to attack in water, so the lake was safe. The people live by fishing and fish farming, and markets are held from boats. With some 20,000 people it is often called the largest lake village in Africa and the Venice of Africa, and it draws tourists from Cotonou. It is a living reminder of how the slave trade shaped where people lived. See also Vodun.
